assertions.name: nuclide_chart_fully_accounted
assertions.source: every AME entry (A>=1): finite-solved, f64-overflow, or build-fail

description: Operator-selection admissibility over the AME2020 chart at q_0. (a) per-nucleus active-channel count = |{i: y*_i>0}| of the H_3 LP dual (prop:operator-selection-lp); (b) permitted-nuclei count = #{(Z,N): Frobenius-demand LP feasible with u_demand = the nucleus's own NF}. Canonical t=TR_M, G=gram_matrix() (no fit); per-nucleus object = build_atom_nf(Z,N).

findings: (a) Active-channel count is CONSTANT (=1) across every f64-finite nucleus under the scalar LP (n_target=A): the H_3-local operator selection just scales with A, so it does NOT discriminate nuclei. Per-nucleus binding richness must live in the tower / Delta_lambda, not the H_3 operator selection.

(b) Naive admissibility does NOT bound the chart: the scalar-LP 'feasible' count equals the f64-finite count (an overflow cutoff, not physics), and the Frobenius equality (Gx=nf AND sum(x)=nf_net, over-determined 7-eq/6-unknown) is degenerate -> 0 feasible. A meaningful 'permitted nuclei at q_0' count needs the PSD-SDP positivity (bound-state) criterion, not the scalar/Frobenius LP.
INFRA: native f64 build_atom_nf overflows for 1337/3558 (~37%) heavy nuclei; an all-nuclides sweep needs the mpfr native path.
